title: Line chart
description:
A line chart draws one or more series over an x axis: `x_column` and `y_column` (or
`y_columns`, or `series_column` for long data). The default style is a braille canvas;
`canvas` picks another pixel grid and `renderer: asciichart` draws box lines.
See `:help dbdash-chart-types`.

query.sql:
WITH RECURSIVE h(n) AS (SELECT 0 UNION ALL SELECT n + 1 FROM h WHERE n < 23)
SELECT printf('%02d:00', n) AS hour, 60 + 40 * sin(n / 3.0) + abs(random() % 20) AS visits,
       (60 + 40 * sin(n / 3.0)) * 0.6 AS mobile, (60 + 40 * sin(n / 3.0)) * 0.4 AS desktop
FROM h

show.title: y_columns, legend, axes (canvas: braille, the default)
show.description:
Three series from `y_columns`, each with a `label` and a `color`; the legend sits on
the `right` (default) or `bottom`; `axes.y_axis` sets a title, `min_value` and a
Python `format` for the tick labels. Braille draws 2 x 4 dots per character.

query.sql:
WITH RECURSIVE h(n) AS (SELECT 0 UNION ALL SELECT n + 1 FROM h WHERE n < 23)
SELECT printf('%02d', n) AS hour, 60 + 40 * sin(n / 3.0) AS visits FROM h

show.title: canvas: quadrant
show.description: `canvas: quadrant`: 2 x 2 pixels per character (▗▄▖), works in most fonts.

query.sql:

SELECT printf('%02d', n) AS hour, 60 + 40 * sin(n / 3.0) AS visits FROM h

show.title: canvas: block
show.description: `canvas: block`: one full block per pixel (coarse but bold).

show.title: canvas: ascii
show.description: `canvas: ascii`: plain ASCII characters, for any terminal or font.

query.sql:
WITH RECURSIVE h(n) AS (SELECT 0 UNION ALL SELECT n + 1 FROM h WHERE n < 23)
SELECT printf('%02d', n) AS hour, 60 + 40 * sin(n / 3.0) AS visits FROM h

show.title: renderer: asciichart
show.description:
`renderer: asciichart` draws the line with box characters (╭─╯) instead of a pixel
canvas. Try it on any line chart with `:DbDashStyle line asciichart`.

query.sql:
WITH RECURSIVE d(n) AS (SELECT 0 UNION ALL SELECT n + 1 FROM d WHERE n < 13)
SELECT printf('%02d', n) AS day, k AS region, 50 + abs(random() % 50) AS orders
FROM d, (SELECT 'EU' AS k UNION ALL SELECT 'US' UNION ALL SELECT 'APAC')

show.title: series_column: long data
show.description:
Long data (one row per x and series) with `series_column`: one line per value of
`region`, colored from the `palette` (`tableau` here; `theme` follows the
colorscheme).

query.sql:
WITH RECURSIVE h(n) AS (SELECT 0 UNION ALL SELECT n + 1 FROM h WHERE n < 11)
SELECT n AS x, 20 + 15 * sin(n / 2.0) AS y FROM h

show.title: line_style: fill_area, show_points
show.description: `fill_area` fills under the line (Chart.js `fill`); `show_points` marks every point.

query.sql:
SELECT 1 AS t, 3 AS level UNION ALL SELECT 2, 3 UNION ALL SELECT 3, 7 UNION ALL SELECT 4, 5
UNION ALL SELECT 5, 9 UNION ALL SELECT 6, 9 UNION ALL SELECT 7, 4

show.title: line_style.stepped
show.description:
Steps instead of slopes (Chart.js `stepped`): `true` / `before` (the value changes
at the start), `after`, `middle`. Good for states and counters.

query.sql:
SELECT 1 AS t, 4 AS v UNION ALL SELECT 2, 6 UNION ALL SELECT 3, NULL UNION ALL SELECT 4, NULL
UNION ALL SELECT 5, 8 UNION ALL SELECT 6, 5 UNION ALL SELECT 7, 7

show.title: line_style: point, span_gaps: false
show.description:
`point` marks each point with a character (Chart.js `pointStyle`); `span_gaps:
false` leaves a gap where the value is NULL instead of joining across it.

query.sql:
WITH RECURSIVE h(n) AS (SELECT 0 UNION ALL SELECT n + 1 FROM h WHERE n < 11)
SELECT n AS month, round(power(2.4, n)) AS users FROM h

show.title: mark_lines, mark_points
show.description:
Reference lines (ECharts `markLine`): a fixed value with a label, or `mean`, `min`,
`max` of the data, on the `y` (default) or `x` axis. `mark_points` labels each
series' `max` and `min` (ECharts `markPoint`).

query.sql:
WITH RECURSIVE h(n) AS (SELECT 0 UNION ALL SELECT n + 1 FROM h WHERE n < 23)
SELECT printf('%02d', n) AS hour, 60 + 40 * sin(n / 3.0) AS visits FROM h

show.title: x_label, y_label, height, width, legend: false
show.description:
`x_label` / `y_label` are short for the axis titles; `height` fixes the plot rows,
`width` caps the chart width; `legend: false` hides the legend.
